title: Wire EDM: arcs in taper (conical) mode

body:
## What happens

A Wire Contour with a taper does not cut a DXF arc as an arc. The selected-chain path refuses a taper on a DXF chain ("selected DXF wire cuts require a single vertical pass"). The wire posts refuse a tapered arc ("a tapered arc - the wire post writes straight tapered moves only"). The verifier reads an arc on a leaning wire as unreadable.

The fix for #3937 cuts vertical arcs as true G2 / G3 arcs. Tapered arcs stay refused on purpose. The maintainer decided that this is rare work (24 Nov 2026).

## Why it is a separate issue

A tapered arc is a cone. The lower and the upper arc have different radii. Each control states a conical arc in its own way. Some controls refuse two arcs in a row in conical mode. Each dialect needs evidence from its control before a post writes such a block.

## What is expected

- The generator lays a tapered arc as a cone: the lower arc and the upper arc, each with its own radius.
- The wire laws and the verifier read the cone against the drawing.
- Each wire post that supports conical arcs writes them. Each other post refuses them by name, as now.

## Related

- #3937 (vertical arcs on DXF chains).
- #3215 (wire output writes no arcs).
- #2702 (G-EDM XYUV taper).

## Labels

The account that files this issue cannot set labels. A collaborator: please set `P8`, `effort:max`, `area:post`, `area:2d`, `source:agent`.

Done means: a tapered DXF arc cuts as a cone on each post that has control evidence, and each other post refuses it by name.
